markdown_content: ## Accessing the STEAM Tool in the 2D Window This section explains where the STEAM tool is located and how to open the STEAM controls from within the 2D window. The **STEAM tool** is inside the **2D window**. Look for a small **iron** icon (the tool indicator) and select it. After selecting it, a **pop-up box** appears, allowing you to start **STEAMing**. ## Core STEAM Parameters: Option Controls (Shrinkage, Size, Hardness) This section covers the main STEAM controls—**shrinkage**, **size**, and **hardness**—and how each one affects the effect you paint onto the garment. Within the STEAM pop-up, you’ll see multiple **options**. The key ones demonstrated are: - **Shrinkage**: Can be set to **negative or positive** (shown as a sign-based behavior in the color preview). - **Size**: Controls the radius of the painted circles. - **Hardness**: Controls how concentrated the effect is at the center versus the edges. ### Size behavior (circle growth/shrink) - Increase **Size** → the circles become **bigger**. - Decrease **Size** → the circles become **smaller**. - The tool displays **two circles**: - The **center circle** corresponds to **hardness**. - The outer circle represents the influence area around the hardness center. ### Hardness behavior (center vs edges) **Hardness** determines how “solid” the effect is at the center, and how it transitions toward the edges. - Higher hardness → the effect spreads **farther outward**. - Lower hardness → the effect is **closer to the center**. - Hardness is described as affecting the **shrinkage percent** concentration at the center, while the edge transition can be “smoothed out” by adjusting hardness. ## Visual Preview: Positive vs Negative (Red vs Blue) and Color Intensity This section describes how positive and negative STEAM values appear in the preview, including how intensity changes across the painted region. When you paint: - **Positive values** (plus) display in **red**. - **Negative values** (minus) display in **blue**. The preview shows a gradient: - The **center** is the strongest (e.g., **dark red** for positive, **dark blue** for negative). - The color becomes **lighter** (orange/light blue) as it moves outward from the center. ## Simulating the Effect on the Garment (Using Simulate) This section explains what happens when you press **simulate**, including how the garment responds to the painted STEAM values. After painting, click **simulate** to see the result on the garment. In the example shown: - The user set **50** for both relevant values and created a region labeled as **puffy** outward and **tight** inward. - The simulation produced visible changes on the shirt, described as the garment “doing weird things” due to the shape changes from the STEAM settings. ## Undo and Clearing STEAM Changes (Control Z) This section explains how to revert STEAM edits and remove previously simulated results using undo. - Press **Ctrl+Z** to undo the last change. - Repeated **Ctrl+Z** steps can: - change out the thing again (reverting the current state), - **unsimulate**, and - remove previously applied STEAM layers/patterns (clearing multiple items one by one). ## Removing STEAM: The Remove Tool and Removal Percentage This section covers how to remove STEAM using the **Remove** option, including percentage-based removal and how repeated clicks affect the outcome. A new update is an option called **Remove**. ### Remove percentage behavior - Click **remove**. - A percentage value (example shown: **70%** default) controls how much STEAM is removed per action. - Example workflow: - Set removal to **30%** - Click **remove** - Result: it removes **about 30%**, not everything. If you want more removed, you must click **remove** again repeatedly. The presenter notes that: - To wipe away faster with fewer clicks, use a **higher number**. - Example given: - At **30%**, multiple swipes/clicks were needed. - At **60%**, the effect was removed in fewer steps (about **two** times in the demo). ### Hardness recommendation for faster clearing To avoid having to constantly keep swiping/removing: - If your STEAM intensity is around **50**, the demo suggests using a **higher removal number** and ensuring **hardness is pretty hard** so removal completes more efficiently. ## Stacking STEAM Layers (Add, Negative Values, and Darkening) This section explains that each click adds another STEAM layer and how repeated application darkens the preview. When using **add**: - Every time you click/paint, it adds **another layer** of STEAM. - The demo shows repeated negative application (example: **negative 42**). - With each additional layer, the painted region becomes **darker** because more layers accumulate. ## Removing STEAM via Right-Click (Selected Pattern or All Steam) This section explains a faster cleanup method using right-click options to remove STEAM without manually erasing layer-by-layer. If you don’t want to erase everything manually: - **Right-click** on the painted area/pattern. - Options shown include: - **Remove steam from selected pattern** (removes steam from the selected area) - **Remove all steam** (removes all STEAM that has been applied) The presenter emphasizes that this right-click removal clears the steam **quickly and easily**.
